description: LONE WOLF is focused on AI, data science, and space exploration. I work with Python, data analysis, machine learning, forecasting, and interactive dashboards. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I aim to turn NASA’s open data into meaningful insights through practical, evidence-based solutions. My interests include Earth science, data visualization, and AI-powered applications. I value independent thinking, analytical problem-solving, and creative ideas.
summary:
EarthTrend is an interactive, browser-based Earth observation and environmental trend investigation platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The platform enables users to explore historical precipitation, air temperature, and relative humidity across selected geographic locations. It combines NASA Earth observation and atmospheric reanalysis resources with interactive maps, time-series visualizations, statistical trend analysis, and regional comparisons.

EarthTrend helps users investigate environmental patterns, compare locations, and understand whether observed trends are statistically significant. It also communicates data limitations and uncertainty to discourage misleading conclusions.

By making Earth science data more accessible and interpretable, EarthTrend aims to support environmental awareness, exploratory research, and evidence-based investigation.
details:
About EarthTrend

EarthTrend is an interactive web-based platform developed to help people investigate environmental patterns and long-term changes using NASA Earth science resources.

The platform provides six main sections:

  1. Earth Overview: Introduces the project and presents an overview of environmental exploration.
  2. Global Explorer: Allows users to select geographic locations and explore historical environmental variables through interactive maps and visualizations.
  3. Trend Analysis: Provides statistical analysis of environmental time series to investigate long-term patterns.
  4. Explore Data: Enables users to inspect and explore the underlying observations.
  5. Regional Comparison: Supports comparisons of precipitation patterns and trends across selected locations.
  6. Methodology: Explains the data sources, processing methods, statistical techniques, and limitations.

NASA Data and Scientific Methodology

EarthTrend uses NASA's POWER Daily API to retrieve environmental data from the following NASA data products:

  • Precipitation: GPM IMERG satellite-derived precipitation estimates (IMERG_PRECTOT).
  • Air Temperature: MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis (T2M).
  • Relative Humidity: MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis (RH2M).

The application also includes an exploratory comparison of GPM IMERG and MERRA-2 precipitation estimates using the MERRA-2 corrected precipitation parameter (PRECTOTCORR).

The platform investigates historical data covering 2001–2025. It uses interactive time-series visualizations, annual and regional comparisons, and statistical techniques including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Theil–Sen slope estimation, and Mann–Kendall trend testing. Confidence intervals and statistical significance assessments help users interpret the strength and uncertainty of observed trends. Multiple-comparison correction is also applied where appropriate.

Intended Benefits and Impact

EarthTrend makes Earth science data more accessible to students, educators, researchers, and the general public. It encourages users to investigate environmental patterns, compare geographic locations, and interpret statistical evidence rather than relying on visual impressions alone.

The platform aims to support environmental awareness, exploratory research, and evidence-based understanding of changes in the Earth's system.

Creativity and Technical Implementation

The project combines interactive geographic exploration, historical environmental data, statistical analysis, and scientific explanations in one browser-based application. Its hybrid interface combines immersive map-focused visualizations with clear scientific information panels.

Technologies used include Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Plotly, PyDeck, and Requests.

Limitations and Responsible Interpretation

EarthTrend uses selected geographic point-based sampling rather than providing continuous, high-resolution global analysis. Data products have their own uncertainties, spatial and temporal characteristics, and limitations. Statistical trends do not establish causation or independently prove climate attribution. Results must therefore be interpreted in the context of their data sources and methodology.

Use of Generative AI

ChatGPT was used as an assistance tool during software development for coding support, debugging, technical problem-solving, and documentation preparation. Generative AI is not integrated into the user-facing application and does not generate, alter, or validate the environmental datasets or scientific findings. Data processing and statistical analyses are performed using the documented methods implemented in the application. The team remains responsible for reviewing the implementation, methodology, and results.
